text.p: Spanish flag carrier Iberia is revising its 1996 profit forecast but should still achieve its first positive net result for eight years, chairman Xabier de Irala said.

The pre-tax profit to the end of August was 10.928 billion pesetas ($84.26 million), and some 30 percent less after tax. Management said earlier this year it expected a 19 billion peseta net profit but this now looks over optimistic.

"It could be a bit less," Irala said, adding that the final figure would easily exceed the 1.5 billion peseta net target in the airline's 1994 viability plan which formed the basis for this year's injection of new capital.
"Iberia is now in a situation of unstable equilibrium and our first task has to be to consolidate our profitability," said Irala who took over as chairman in July.
The company's second task was to seal a partnership with one or more foreign airlines.
"A strategic alliance for Iberia is absolutely necessary," he told journalists, but gave no new details of who these partners could be.

Iberia has been in detailed conversations with British Airways Plc and KLM and with a number of U.S. carriers for some time but none of these talks has yet come close to forming the basis of such a partnership.
